title: Rent-Period Fitting of the Company Cap — Lease Term Agreement Renewal Worksheet
content:
On a like-program renewal offer line of a Lease Term Agreement, the company cap, once fully determined, is fitted to the rent period, and it is this rent-period cap that is compared with the statutory increase cap of the community's state, the lower of the two being the effective cap.

## The rent period

The rent period is the days the in-place rent will have been in force at the end of the expiring term, counted from the effective date of the last rent change recorded on the term (or from the term start date when none is recorded) through the term end date, both days included.

## Fitting

| Rent period | Rent-period cap |
|---|---|
| Shorter than 365 days | The company cap prorated: the company cap multiplied by the rent period's days and divided by 365 |
| 365 to 729 days | The company cap as it stands |
| 730 days or longer | The company cap compounded over two years: one plus the company cap, squared, less one |

No figure in the fitting is rounded.

## Worked cases (hypothetical company cap of 6 percent)

| Rent in force from | Term end date | Rent period | Rent-period cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 January | 19 July of the same non-leap year | 200 days | 6 percent multiplied by 200 and divided by 365: about 3.2877 percent (unrounded) |
| 1 January | 31 December of the same non-leap year | 365 days | 6 percent |
| 1 January | 30 December of the following non-leap year | 729 days | 6 percent |
| 1 January | 31 December of the following non-leap year | 730 days | one plus 0.06 is 1.06; squared is 1.1236; less one: 12.36 percent |

In the last case, in a Washington community the rent-period cap of 12.36 percent exceeds the statutory 9.68 percent, so 9.68 percent governs; in a Colorado community, with no statutory cap, 12.36 percent governs.
